ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a cyclic ozonide/primary ozonide-like structure containing three oxygen atoms; the two lower carbon atoms on the left and right each are connected to two methyl substituents; there are multiple curved arrows in the image, indicating electron-pair movement, accompanied by rearrangement and cleavage of intraring bonds. Reasoning: According to the electron migration shown by the curved arrows, one lower dimethyl-substituted carbon forms an ordinary carbonyl, and the product is acetone, with SMILES CC(C)=O. The other lower dimethyl-substituted carbon forms a carbonyl oxide zwitterionic fragment, namely C=[O+][O-], whose SMILES is CC(C)=[O+][O-]. The problem asks to write the molecular state after electron relocation, so a dot is used to separate the two species.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows a symmetric dimethyl-substituted ozonide/molozonide-type structure with curved arrows indicating simultaneous electron relocation and cleavage. Follow each arrow literally to update the bonding: one lower carbon becomes a normal C=O ketone with two methyl groups, giving acetone, CC(C)=O. The other lower carbon remains attached to two methyl groups and becomes a carbonyl oxide/zwitterionic C=[O+][O-] unit, giving CC(C)=[O+][O-]. Because the question asks for the state after the depicted electron relocation, list the two separated molecular species with a dot separator: CC(C)=O.CC(C)=[O+][O-].

Combine the two product SMILES separated by a period to represent separate molecules: CC(C)=O.CC(C)=[O+][O-].
